architecture.summary: The hosted image workflow of SO-01b becomes the release path (SO-02): each push to main builds Dockerfile.hosted for linux/amd64 on a GitHub-hosted runner, runs the hosted image gate on that image, and pushes it to GHCR by digest, and a failed check or gate pushes nothing. A new deploy job runs only on a manual dispatch on main with a digest and a Render service ID; with the repository secret RENDER_API_KEY of a dedicated Render user (Member of Thermus AI; no GitHub environment), it checks that GHCR has the digest, calls the Render API deploy with imageUrl, waits for live, checks the digest in the live deploy and in imagePath, and checks /healthz on the public URL. It refuses another branch, a service outside Thermus AI, a service that is not an image-backed web service, and the production service without confirm_production. This adds a delivery relationship from GitHub Actions to Render and gives the workflows of this repository deploy authority over the Thermus AI workspace, production included: deployment and crossCutting. Each merge now runs the hosted image gate, a release process change: policy. Production still builds from Git with autoDeploy off until step 5 of SO-12, so no C4 container, runtime relationship, contract, component, or Mermaid view changes; the registry deployment view gains prose for the release path. GHCR keeps every running digest and the last ten release digests, with a monthly pruning step in README.
